sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier labrum rather long and narrow, nearly semi-elliptical; mandibles rather short, curved toward the apex and acute, the base of the right mandible with two fairly large teeth, the left lower mandible with two large teeth near the middle; antenna 15-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2. It differs from the congeneric L. laticephalus in the narrow, elongate labrum and the two teeth at the base of the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: labrum rather long, slightly narrow, nearly semi-elliptical. Mandibles rather short, curved toward the apex and acute; the base of the right mandible with two fairly large teeth, the left mandible with two large teeth near the middle. Antenna 15-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2. Measurements: body length 9.5 mm.

note: Adapted from Silvestri's 1901 "Nota preliminare sui Termitidi sud-americani" (in Latin), where the species was named Cornitermes orthocephalus sp. n. and only brief diagnostic characters of the soldier and the body length were given, without itemized measurements; type locality Coxipò (Cuyabá), Brazil. Snyder (1949) placed the species in Paracornitermes; since 2000 it has mostly been placed in Labiotermes.
